speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where your wrist pain is located and what specific movements make it difficult to use your hand.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The history of a fall six months ago, combined with pain radiating from the thumb to the wrist that worsens with lifting an infant (a classic aggravating factor for thumb extension), strongly suggests a diagnosis of De Quervain's Tenosynovitis or potentially a Chronic Wrist Extensor Tendinopathy. The family history of rheumatoid arthritis is notable but less likely given the specific mechanical nature of the pain. I will confirm this with a specific orthopedic test.
